question: Who among the following Bahmani sultans transferred his capital from Gulbarga to Bidar?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Ahmad Shah**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ahmad Shah I,** the **ninth sultan of the Bahmani Sultanate,** made a significant decision in **1422 **by relocating the **capital from Gulbarga to Bidar**.
 
• This move was motivated by Bidar's strategic advantages, including its more favorable climate and central location.
 
• **Bidar** was surrounded by fertile land and became even more centrally situated after the acquisition of territory to the southeast in Telingana.
 
• Ahmad Shah I's reign heralded the transition from the Gulbarga phase to the Bidar phase of the Bahmani kingdom.
 
• Under his rule, the **Bahmani Sultanate **experienced a shift in focus towards expansionism and military campaigns.
 
• Ahmad Shah I converted to Shi'ism, marking a religious change within the ruling elite.
 
• His reign was characterized by efforts to strengthen and expand the kingdom's territories, setting the stage for significant developments in the Bahmani Sultanate's history.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• **Ahmad Shah I, **originally known as Ahmad Khan, was a significant ruler of the Muzaffarid dynasty, governing the **Gujarat Sultanate from 1411** until his passing in 1442.
 
• He was the grandson of Sultan Muzaffar Shah, the dynasty's founder.
 
• Ahmad Shah I is renowned as the founder of Ahmedabad, the most populous city in Gujarat, which bears his name.
 
• Besides his administrative accomplishments, he was also a notable poet, having composed a collection of Persian poetry.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Humayun,** the second Mughal emperor, ruled over vast territories spanning Eastern Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Northern India, and Pakistan from 1530 to 1540 and again from 1555 until his death in 1556.
 
• **Mujahid Shah Bahmani **ascended to the throne as the 3rd Sultan of the Bahmani Sultanate, playing a significant role in its governance and development.
 
• **Sultan Firuz Shah Tughlaq,** hailing from the Tughlaq dynasty, was a prominent Muslim ruler who reigned over the Sultanate of Delhi from 1351 to 1388, leaving a lasting impact on the region's history and administration.
